correctness.rationale: For every integer d≥2 and every normalized step 0<γ<2, expanding the actual forward differences in a Haar full basis gives X_next=(1−γ)X−aV, with a=γδ√d/2 and V uniform on the unit sphere. The geometric random series converges absolutely and is the unique stationary law; synchronous coupling gives the exact Wasserstein contraction. The polygon inequality and connectedness of spheres (d≥2) identify every attainable radius, yielding the sharp closed annulus/ball/sphere support. Independent zero-mean increments give dγδ²/[4(2−γ)] exactly. Addition of two nonparallel independent sphere vectors has a full-rank derivative almost everywhere, establishing absolute continuity when γ≠1. The packaged checker passed 780 exact rational checks, 750 independent finite-difference tests and five stationary diagnostics. The nonstandard support and regularity steps have explicit proof in RESULT.md; no finite test is treated as an infinite proof.

limitations: No general theorem for other objective functions or reduced-batch sketches.
The support statement describes possible stationary errors, not their probabilities or finite-time confidence intervals.
value.rationale: Constant-step forward finite differences are a standard practical zeroth-order choice, yet norm/expectation bounds do not determine whether stationary iterates can approach the optimizer at all. The theorem identifies the exact missing central ball for an entire open stepsize region, its reentrant return to full support for both smaller and larger stable steps, and the isolated spherical state at the exact-gradient cancellation step. It shows that the worst supported deviation can remain at a fixed nonzero radius even while the stationary mean-square error tends to zero. These are sharp, all-dimensional structural constraints on one concrete algorithm and provide a reproducible benchmark for confidence and tuning; the result is not a claim of overall algorithmic superiority.
